name: Computer control
summary: Lets Alexia see what is on screen, press things, move the mouse and type. Anything a person at this keyboard could do.

requires.why: To see your screen — a picture of it, and the list of what is on it and where.
To press things, move the mouse, click, and type on your keyboard as if you were doing it.
To ask the computer itself to do those things — PowerShell on Windows, osascript on a Mac.
To put the screenshots somewhere. They are deleted when you delete this plugin.
Only when TypeSafe Jev decides: to send your goal and the names of the controls on screen to api.typesafe.ai.

settings.label: Allow it to press things, move the mouse and type
settings.hint: Off means it can look but not touch — no pressing, no pointer, no keyboard. Looking still works, and it is the useful half most of the time. Turn this on only while you are watching.

settings.label: Who decides each step
settings.hint: Alexia's model is how it has always worked: the chat model reads the screen and chooses every step itself. Jev is a separate, much faster model that only chooses — the next control from the list on screen, with how sure it is — and stops and hands back when it is not sure. The words it types still come from Alexia's model.

options.label: Alexia's model
options.hint: The chat model drives, one turn per step. Nothing new to sign up for.

options.label: TypeSafe Jev
options.hint: Needs a TypeSafe key. Each step sends your goal and the names of the controls in the window to TypeSafe, and costs a fraction of a cent.

settings.label: TypeSafe key
settings.hint: Only used when Jev decides. From console.typesafe.ai. It goes to this machine's credential store, never to the database.

settings.label: Screenshots to keep
settings.hint: Older ones are deleted. Zero keeps none after the call that made them.

widgets.label: Saved sequences
widgets.hint: The same five clicks, without paying a model to work them out again. A plan with no decision in it has no model in its path at all.
